# 4 Maccabees Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Eleazar's Martyrdom

---

**6:1** When Eleazar was brought before the tribunal and the soldiers had bound him, they commanded him again to eat of the forbidden meat.

**6:2** But Eleazar, as a man of noble character who gave no sign of dishonor, spoke out boldly:

**6:3** We will not be compelled so easily, Antiochus, into eating the unclean food; for the law is our schoolmaster, and we are persuaded that it speaks truth.

**6:4** When the guards had brought him to the rack and torn his sides open with hooks, trying to force the meat into his mouth through his open wounds,

**6:5** Eleazar did not yield. Instead, though he was being scourged, he raised his eyes to heaven and said:

**6:6** You know, O God, that though I could have saved myself, I am dying in burning torments for the sake of the law.

**6:7** Be merciful to your people and let my punishment be a satisfaction on their behalf.

**6:8** Make my blood their purification, and take my soul as a ransom for their souls.

**6:9** Having said this, the holy man died nobly in his torments, enduring by the power of reason that was rooted in piety even the ordeal of fire.

**6:10** Eleazar was thus the first to enter the way of the holy martyrs.

**6:11** Eleazar the priest had fixed his eyes on God and made his soul one with the noble death of martyrdom; his soul, like an athlete, held firm against the blows.

**6:12** He endured the ordeal not because he was compelled but because he was devoted.

**6:13** O sacred striving of a holy soul! O noble endurance of the philosopher! O victory of piety over passion!

**6:14** O Eleazar! Most noble of wrestlers! You were not moved by the cruelty of the tyrant's threats, nor were you burned from your purpose by the fire.

**6:15** Noble athlete of the divine law! You were fitted not with armor of stone or iron but with the unbreakable armor of devotion, and through it you conquered the enemy.

**6:16** In you, O father, the law proved its sovereignty — for through the power of holy reason you showed clearly that reason is master of the passions.

**6:17** O Eleazar! You did not defile your sacred mouth by tasting the forbidden flesh, nor did you yield to your appetite even though your body was burning.

**6:18** You maintained the holy beauty of your old age, preserving it through the nobility of your choices.

**6:19** For in you the wisdom of the law proved that reason is truly sovereign over passion.

**6:20** Holy and honored is the death of those who die for the sake of the law.

**6:21** Truly blessed are you, Eleazar — you have received the incorruptible prizes of immortality.

**6:22** For you lit the lamp of devotion for all Israel that day, and your endurance shone out like a beacon for all who came after you.

**6:23** He had lived ninety years and was not weakened by the pleasures of the body but remained strong through reason.

**6:24** While the fire was blazing around him and the tormentors were applying their instruments, he withstood everything with a fixed gaze and an unconquerable soul.

**6:25** O priest clothed in the priestly garment of philosophy! O elder devoted to the holy law! O life of the holy man faithful to the ancient ways!

**6:26** Through such nobility, Eleazar became the pioneer of those who die for the sake of piety.

**6:27** Through the devotion of this man, the suffering of Israel was sanctified and the tyranny over the nation was overcome.

**6:28** For the suffering that Eleazar endured was sufficient to sanctify the nation.

**6:29** Even the king himself was stopped in his tracks and held back from advancing further against the holy city because of what this man's death had shown.

**6:30** And thus through the nobility of his death, Eleazar became the beginning of purification for all of Israel.
